\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{على} \ar{الفور} (ʿalā al-fawr)}{على الفور (ʿalā al-fawr)}]{\ar{على} \ar{الفور} (ʿalā al-fawr) — on the spot, at once}

\label{lesson:AR-C313-ala-al-fawr}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an explorer, then the Arabic for a treasure.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{على} \ar{الفور}}
\textbf{\ar{على} \ar{الفور}} — \emph{ʿalā al-fawr} — \textquotedblleft{}on the spot, at once\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{اتصلت} \ar{بالطبيب} \ar{على} \ar{الفور}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ittaṣaltu bi-ṭ-ṭabīb ʿalā al-fawr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I called the doctor at once.
\end{quote}

The taught \ar{فورا} is the same word as an adverb.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{على} \ar{الفور}} (\emph{ʿalā al-fawr}) is \textquotedblleft{}on the boiling\textquotedblright{}: \emph{fawr} is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-w-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to boil, to gush\textquotedblright{} (Lane), the root of the taught \emph{fawran}. What is done at the boil is done at once.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿalā al-fawr}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿalā al-fawr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ittaṣaltu bi-ṭ-ṭabīb ʿalā al-fawr.} — I called the doctor at once.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an explorer, then the Arabic for a treasure, then say \emph{ʿalā al-fawr} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{على} \ar{الفور} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}On the spot, at once\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{سرعان} \ar{ما} (surʿāna mā)}{سرعان ما (surʿāna mā)}]{\ar{سرعان} \ar{ما} (surʿāna mā) — before long, soon after}

\label{lesson:AR-C313-suraana-ma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a treasure, then the Arabic for on the spot.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{سرعان} \ar{ما}}
\textbf{\ar{سرعان} \ar{ما}} — \emph{surʿāna mā} — \textquotedblleft{}before long, soon after\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{بدأ} \ar{المطر} \ar{وسرعان} \ar{ما} \ar{توقف}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{badaʾa al-maṭar wa-surʿāna mā tawaqqafa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The rain began and soon stopped.
\end{quote}

A past verb follows it: \ar{سرعان} \ar{ما} \ar{عاد}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{سرعان} \ar{ما}} (\emph{surʿāna mā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-r-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to be quick\textquotedblright{} (Lane), the root of \emph{surʿa}, speed: \emph{surʿāna} means \textquotedblleft{}how quick!\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{surʿāna mā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{surʿāna mā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{badaʾa al-maṭar wa-surʿāna mā tawaqqafa.} — The rain began and soon stopped.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a treasure, then the Arabic for on the spot, then say \emph{surʿāna mā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{سرعان} \ar{ما} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Before long, soon after\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تدريجيا} (tadrījiyyan)}{تدريجيا (tadrījiyyan)}]{\ar{تدريجيا} (tadrījiyyan) — gradually, step by step}

\label{lesson:AR-C313-tadrijiyyan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for on the spot, then the Arabic for before long.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تدريجيا}}
\textbf{\ar{تدريجيا}} — \emph{tadrījiyyan} — \textquotedblleft{}gradually, step by step\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تحسن} \ar{الطقس} \ar{تدريجيا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taḥassana aṭ-ṭaqs tadrījiyyan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The weather gradually got better.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تدريجيا}} (\emph{tadrījiyyan}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{d-r-j} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to walk step by step\textquotedblright{}, the root of \emph{daraja}, a step. \emph{Tadrīj} is the verbal noun of Form II; \emph{-iyyan} makes it an adverb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tadrījiyyan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tadrījiyyan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taḥassana aṭ-ṭaqs tadrījiyyan.} — The weather gradually got better.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for on the spot, then the Arabic for before long, then say \emph{tadrījiyyan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تدريجيا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Gradually, step by step\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{من} \ar{جديد} (min jadīd)}{من جديد (min jadīd)}]{\ar{من} \ar{جديد} (min jadīd) — anew, all over again}

\label{lesson:AR-C313-min-jadid}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for before long, then the Arabic for gradually.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{من} \ar{جديد}}
\textbf{\ar{من} \ar{جديد}} — \emph{min jadīd} — \textquotedblleft{}anew, all over again\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{بدأ} \ar{الطلاب} \ar{الدرس} \ar{من} \ar{جديد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{badaʾa aṭ-ṭullāb ad-dars min jadīd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The students started the lesson all over again.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{من} \ar{جديد}} (\emph{min jadīd}) is \textquotedblleft{}from new\textquotedblright{}: \emph{min} with the taught \emph{jadīd}, new, which is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-d-d} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استعاد} (istaʿāda)}{استعاد (istaʿāda)}]{\ar{استعاد} (istaʿāda) — to regain, to get back}

\label{lesson:AR-C313-istaada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for gradually, then the Arabic for anew.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استعاد}}
\textbf{\ar{استعاد}} — \emph{istaʿāda} — \textquotedblleft{}to regain, to get back\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{استعاد} \ar{الرجل} \ar{حقيبته} \ar{من} \ar{الشرطة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{istaʿāda ar-rajul ḥaqībatahu min ash-shurṭa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The man got his bag back from the police.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يستعيد}, \emph{yastaʿīd}.

\ar{استعاد} \ar{ذكرياته}: he went back over his memories.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{استعاد}} (\emph{istaʿāda}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-w-d} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to return\textquotedblright{}, the root of \emph{ʿāda}, he came back. It is Form X, \textquotedblleft{}to seek the return of\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istaʿāda}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istaʿāda}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istaʿāda ar-rajul ḥaqībatahu min ash-shurṭa.} — The man got his bag back from the police.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for gradually, then the Arabic for anew, then say \emph{istaʿāda} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{استعاد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To regain, to get back\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
